content.text:
From: Thomas, Christopher
Sent: Monday, February 11, 2019 3:50 PM
To: Fenech, Anthony
Subject: Tigers spring training 
 
Anthony: Here’s a rundown of important dates, ideas for weekly content and just general thoughts on stories as spring training heats up over the next month. One thing we’ve got to be better is working and filing those weekly digital pieces to us the night before (Lakeland letters, prospects, mailbags, etc.). I want you to flourish this year, and the only way for me to show that is through digital audience growth.

With that said, here’s where I’m at on preview content, other things. The preview section is sort of set in stone, though I suppose we could tweak things sooner than later if you feel it’s necessary. I’m open to discussion on any of the other topics as well.

We’re NOT doing a special section this year. Instead, we’ll publish most of our preview content in print heading into the opener on MARCH 28. Here’s what I’m considering for that section … please let me know if you want to add or subtract anything. The deadline for all section content is 8 A.M. March 25.

=DFP TIGERS CABRERA: Fenech, on the reconstruction of Tigers star Miguel Cabrera. This could be our blowout piece in print. Who’s “the new Miggy.” Don’t be afraid to talk about off-field drama and how it has impacted him. Or his big contract. Or how fans will handle this new Miggy.
**=DFP PITCH PROSPECTS: Fenech or Seidel … something deep on the pitching prospects of Mize, Perez etc. Maybe this runs with preview content. Maybe earlier.** (**tentative)
=DFP MEET TIGERS: Fenech, meet the players on the 25-man roster. Last year we listed …

=TIGERS THREE QUESTIONS: Fenech, Seidel, Windsor, Ford … answer three pressing question. 1. How many games will the Tigers lose. 2. Which prospect will make the biggest impact? 3. Who will be the Tigers’ All-Star selection? INSTRUCTIONS: Please proved 50-word answer to each question.

=DFP FENECH PREDICTIONS: Fenech and Ford, predict order of finish for each division in baseball (i.e. for AL Central … 1. Indians, 2. White Sox, 3. Tigers, etc.). Also need predictions for the following:
AL Wild Card: Angels over Yankees
NL Wild Card: xxx over xxx
ALDS: xxx over xxxx; xxx over xxx
NLDS: xxx over xxx; xxxx over xxx
=DFP TIGERS SCHEDULE: Ryan Ford, like last season.
=DFP TIGERS BUZZ: Ryan Ford, buzz on what should be an ‘L’ of a season.
=DFP AL CENTRAL: Ford or wires, breaking down the other AL Central teams.

Anthony: I want us to establish a flow of weekly content for the web. Lakeland Letters are a GREAT idea. And I agree the podcast is a must-have on a weekly basis (we’re in the process of monetizing them, so they need to happen every week).

IMPORTANT: I need all programmable content filed the night before so I we can publish it at 6 a.m. the next morning. Please adjust your workflow to make this happen. (two exceptions: Podcast can be filed by 10 a.m. … and the live chats will go at an agreed-upon time)

=WEEKLY PROSPECT RANKINGS: I want this to be fun and lighthearted, like the Lakeland Letters. Rif on the past week, the good and bad prospect performances (or just some funny prospect moments) and then give me your updated top 10 prospects at the end with a short explanation why for each player. I think this can do big traffic for us this spring. This might make sense for Wednesdays (would need this ready to post at 6 a.m.)
=LIVE CHATS/MAILBAGS: I think we alternate these each Friday. For instance, a mailbag would be ready to publish at 6 a.m. one Friday … but a live chat could happen during a game on another Friday.
So, the week could look like:

A list of ideas that have popped in my head, in no order. I’m sure there will be many more than this: 
Once Machado and Harper sign … send us a list of power rankings that we can make into a gallery. 
Is Michael Fulmer just an injury-prone pitcher? And are the Tigers doing anything to help him prevent injuries (i.e. his delivery). 
Casey Mize’s timeline to MLB 
Where Franklin Perez stands after injury-plagued year (what do scouts say?)
Daz Cameron’s timeline to MLB
Predicting Tigers’ opening day roster in 2019
Predicting Tigers’ opening day roster in 2021
List of where notable Tigers prospects not at camp are in their development (Faedo comes to mind). 
Deeper dive comparing state of Tigers’ rebuild to some recent ones (expounding on what you did with the Phillies the other day). Also … look at parallels to Mets, others who chose to build pitching staff first … similar to Tigers. 
Good call on Greiner feature. 
Christin Stewart’s defensive development … or just the raw power … but where he fits in this season and beyond
Tell me what the hell the Tigers should do with the bullpen and the rotation. Could be a column on each. “Here’s what the Tigers should do …”
Joe Jimenez … when is it now or never? It’s like four straight years of ‘when is this dude going to be the closer of the future?’ Could be another column.
Organizational depth chart you and Dana discussed (could go after spring training) … maybe the first Sunday of the season? Could do a doubletruck. 
Use your news judgement, but this gives you an idea of where my head is at. I like stories that explain “how” or “why” something happened, more so than just “what” happened.
